question: why does score2 lag score1, and why do the anti arms outrun the pro arms
answer: aggregate structure: min is a conjunction and saturates; max is a disjunction and does not

matched_iteration_live_abs.note: |LIVE| = |sign*(best board so far - baseline)|; matched iterations, so hardware differences do not enter

anti_over_pro_ratio.attribution: ~1.6x geometric (visible with the aggregate held fixed), ~1.9x extra from min->max

withdrawn.claim: T_SA runs ~3.4x hotter on score2 because its steps are 3.4x smaller (commit 9517e05)
withdrawn.why_wrong: measured only over iter>=384. Through iter 300 the two arms have near-identical median step sizes (5.99e-4 vs 6.27e-4), so the temperature was equally scaled. score2's small late steps are a CONSEQUENCE of saturation, not its cause.
withdrawn.status: the --t-sa-scale flag and job 706969 remain a valid experiment (does cooling improve retention on a saturated objective?) but the stated mechanism was backwards.

also_withdrawn.claim: score2's min creates a flat search landscape
also_withdrawn.why_wrong: score2-hardmin has 3.6% identical consecutive states vs score1's 5.0% -- less flat, not more.

corrupted_submission.cause: the prompt contains two real newline bytes (0x0a 0x0a); it was copied from a Python repr so they arrived as literal backslash-n text, plus an inserted newline. 38 tokens submitted vs 32 in the run.
